papers.title: Single-channel EEG denoising and artifact removal: A systematic scoping review of methods, benchmarking, and reproducibility.
papers.summary: A systematic scoping review of 178 articles describing 199 single-channel-compatible EEG artifact-removal method variants, mapping operating paradigms, artifact coverage, evaluation design, and reproducibility. Most variants were reference-free at inference (179/199) and evaluation centered on controlled signal reconstruction (known-target fidelity for 170/199), with only 18 learned variants tested on external data and no deployment evidence for 122/199.

papers.title: Unsupervised functional stage detection from EEG using topological data analysis.
papers.summary: Introduces a topological data analysis (TDA) feature engineering approach for unsupervised EEG functional stage detection, including a quick state-detecting algorithm (QSDA). Applied to meditation and sleep EEG, TDA-derived features produced well-separated stage boundaries and appeared to complement or outperform spectral features in some settings.

papers.title: Resolution-aware spectral parameterization reveals robust context-dependent aperiodic EEG dynamics during real-world table tennis
papers.summary: Analyzing the OpenNeuro Real World Table Tennis dataset from 25 participants with EEG, noise-layer, EMG, and motion recordings, this study used artifact-informed residualization and resolution-aware spectral parameterization to compare peri-hit spectral activity between human-opponent and ball-machine play. Residualized alpha and beta power was lower during ball-machine play, and the clearest context difference was a higher aperiodic exponent over posterior and parietal sensors during ball-machine play, with a focal parietal effect persisting across specifications.

papers.title: Protocol for chronic electroencephalography, fiber photometry, and silicon probe recordings in the Syrian hamster.
papers.summary: The paper presents a step-by-step protocol for chronic surgical implantation and multimodal neuronal recordings in Syrian hamsters, including EEG, fiber photometry, and multi-channel silicon probe recordings. It addresses the lack of detailed protocols for chronic neuronal measurements in this species, which is a model for metabolic control and brain-state transitions.

papers.title: Detecting EEG index of arousal in sleeping patients with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome.
papers.summary: Nighttime polysomnography in patients with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, minimally conscious state patients, and healthy controls showed that EEG spectral slope fluctuated with sleep stages and indexed arousal across all groups, whereas spectral entropy and Lempel-Ziv complexity indexed awareness and differed significantly between conscious and unconscious states. The findings support the two-component hypothesis of consciousness, separating arousal from awareness.

papers.title: CANDLE: Cortical Null-Space Decomposition for Noninvasive Brain Source Imaging
papers.summary: Proposes CANDLE, a learning-based electrophysiological source imaging model that learns a prior over the null space of the source-to-sensor mapping from subject-specific T1-weighted MRI, restricting learning to unobservable source components while preserving geometric constraints. Trained only on simulated data from over 1,100 cortical geometries, CANDLE outperformed prior ESI methods on simulated source estimation and generalized to intracranial stimulation localization and epileptogenic zone estimation from scalp EEG.

papers.title: EEG signatures at ascending vs descending propofol vs sevoflurane concentrations analyzed with BIS and a State-Chart Score
papers.summary: The study analyzed EEG patterns during propofol and sevoflurane anesthesia in 89 patients and introduced a State-Chart representation that maps EEG activity into discrete depth states. The State-Chart showed significantly lower temporal variability than BIS (0.5 ± 0.6 vs 4.0 ± 2.9; p<10^-90) and better discriminated stable versus transition regimes and identical concentration levels.

papers.title: Feature-Engineering Strategies for EEG-Based ADHD Classification in Children: A Controlled Benchmark of Expert, LLM-Guided and Full-Space Comparators
papers.summary: Benchmarks expert, LLM-guided, and full-space EEG feature strategies for pediatric ADHD classification under leakage-controlled subject-level validation. Expert-reconstructed features achieved the highest accuracy and balanced accuracy for every classifier, while LLM-guided selection showed no consistent advantage; a 200 V artifact gate reduced accuracy below the no-information rate.

papers.title: Improving RSVP EEG Decoding Performance under Auditory Perturbation: A Dual-View Model with Robust Distillation.
papers.summary: The paper proposes TFDV-Net, a time-frequency dual-view network with dual-stream knowledge distillation, to improve RSVP-EEG decoding under auditory perturbation. The method achieved balanced accuracies of 83.02% and 80.78% under urban and conversational noise, respectively, outperforming the state-of-the-art baseline by 3.27% and 4.36%.

papers.title: Involuntary facial muscle activity during imagined vocalisation contaminates EEG and enables emotion decoding
papers.summary: This study investigated EEG-based emotion decoding during overt and imagined emotional vocalisation, finding single-trial decoding accuracies of 78.1% for overt and 36.4% for imagined vocalisation, with high-gamma and lateral channels being important. Concurrent facial sEMG revealed that involuntary muscle activity, especially a 'railroad cross-tie' pattern during imagined happy vocalisation, contaminates EEG and contributes to decoding, cautioning similar emotion decoding studies.

papers.title: A comprehensive physiological dataset of pain and aversive modalities for pain biomarkers research
papers.summary: Presents a multimodal physiological dataset from 125 pain-free adults with EEG plus behavioral, sociodemographic, and psychological measures, and galvanic skin response and ECG in a subset of 76, using two painful (thermal, chemical) and two non-painful aversive (auditory, taste) sustained stimulations each delivered twice. Technical validation showed spectral and physiological responses tracking stimulus intensity and subjective pain/unpleasantness, supporting biomarker development and validation.

papers.title: EEGDM: Learning EEG Representation with Latent Diffusion Model.
papers.summary: The paper introduces EEGDM, a self-supervised framework that uses latent diffusion models to generate EEG signals as a training objective, capturing global temporal patterns and cross-channel relationships. Experimental results show that EEGDM reconstructs high-quality EEG signals, learns robust representations, and achieves competitive performance across diverse downstream tasks.

papers.title: Quantitative EEG in typical absence seizures: a systematic review of spectral and entropy/complexity signatures.
papers.summary: A systematic review of 26 reports (449 patient-records; 21 non-overlapping cohorts) synthesizing quantitative EEG spectral and entropy/complexity signatures in typical absence seizures. Pre-ictal slow-band scalp-spectral elevation was concordant across cohorts (delta increased in 4 of 5) and ictal entropy decreased in 5 of 5 cohorts, while interictal patient-versus-control contrasts were heterogeneous and supported no generalized deficit.

papers.title: Spectrally-resolved transfer entropy in resting-state SEEG reveals epileptogenic and non-epileptogenic communication in adults and children with refractory epilepsy.
papers.summary: Characterizes directed, spectrally-resolved communication between seizure onset zones (SOZ) and non-involved zones using resting-state SEEG transfer entropy in adults and children with refractory epilepsy. Finds multiplex cross-frequency interactions, with longer NIZ-to-SOZ delays in adults and distinct SOZ-to-SOZ spectral patterns between cohorts.

papers.title: Altered Aperiodic EEG Activity in Adolescents with Neurofibromatosis Type 1
papers.summary: This study compared resting-state EEG aperiodic exponent (1/f) in 16 adolescents with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 and 16 matched neurotypical controls, finding a higher aperiodic exponent in the NF1 group, consistent with increased inhibitory tone. The NF1 group also showed lower dominant oscillatory frequency, with no significant association between aperiodic exponent and cognitive performance.

papers.title: Emotional Context Modulates Neural Prediction-Error Encoding.
papers.summary: This EEG study examined how emotional context modulates neural prediction-error (PE) encoding during reinforcement learning using a drifting three-armed bandit task with emotional images. Trialwise analyses showed that emotional context significantly moderated the relationship between PE and feedback-locked neural activity, with the strongest PE-EEG relationship in neutral contexts and attenuation in positive (early RewP) and negative (later posterior) contexts, while condition-averaged analyses showed minimal emotional effects.

papers.title: Strain-Decoupled Serpentine Heterostructured Hydrogel Electrodes for Motion-Artifact-Resistant Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: The authors developed a strain-decoupled serpentine heterostructured hydrogel electrode (SHGE) that suppresses motion artifacts by localizing deformation away from the sensing interface. The SHGE exhibited high fracture energy (23.4 kJ/m2), stable electrical output over 50,000 bending cycles, and strain-insensitive operation up to 70% deformation, enabling high-fidelity EMG/ECG with higher SNR than commercial electrodes and >90% accuracy in classifying eight human motions when integrated with machine learning.

papers.title: Kinestesia: the prefrontal EEG response to a cognitive-motor intervention is graded by baseline cognitive status.
papers.summary: This companion neurophysiological study of the Kinestesia cognitive-motor intervention analyzed resting-state EEG before and after 30 sessions in 19 older adults (10 healthy controls, 9 with mild cognitive impairment). Eight of eleven prespecified EEG indices showed a Benjamini-Hochberg-corrected association with baseline MoCA, with the strongest effects for the Engagement Index and Alpha/Beta Ratio at Fp2, indicating that the electrocortical response was graded by baseline cognitive status.

papers.title: Reducing cognitive demand fails to mitigate choice overload: Multimodal neural and gaze evidence for effort conservation.
papers.summary: Two experiments manipulating cognitive demand (via high-attractiveness option sets or a shortlist tool) while recording eye-tracking and EEG found that reducing demand accelerated decisions but did not improve choice performance as set size increased. Multimodal evidence indicated effort conservation: narrower visual search, shorter fixation-related ERP latencies, and weaker occipital alpha suppression under low demand, leaving choice overload intact.

papers.title: Movement and Frontal Theta Activity During Step-Based Exergaming in Healthy Younger and Older Adults: Laboratory-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional laboratory study examined how movements and frontal theta activity relate to game performance in a step-based exergame across younger and older adults. Game scores were strongly correlated with movement amount (r=0.67-0.80) but not consistently with frontal theta activity, suggesting scores primarily reflect movement output rather than cognitive-control demands.

papers.title: Temporal expectation triggers priority shifts in working memory that lead to forgetting.
papers.summary: Using multivariate pattern analysis of EEG in 20 human participants, this study tracked neural representations of two working memory items (face and scene) across short and long delays. Forgetting of deprioritized items was associated with decreased neural evidence for those items and concurrent increased neural evidence for newly prioritized items, demonstrating that temporal expectation-driven priority shifts in working memory predict long-term memory outcomes.

papers.title: An adaptive technical and behavioral approach for biomarker acquisition in autism with intellectual disability
papers.summary: The paper presents a participant-centered protocol combining adaptive EEG and eye-tracking with individualized behavioral supports to acquire biomarkers in autistic children with intellectual disability. Feasibility testing in 76 ASD+ID children yielded usable EEG data (>7 min) in 61% and sufficient eye-tracking data in 67%, demonstrating that inclusive biomarker acquisition is feasible in this underserved population.

papers.title: Acute Whole-Body Heat Exposure Modulates EEG Microstate Dynamics, Phase-Lagged Connectivity, and Cortical Source Activity.
papers.summary: Fifteen healthy men underwent 45-minute seated exposures at 21, 30, and 38 °C while EEG and thermal measures were recorded. Increasing ambient temperature was associated with a shift toward lower EEG frequencies, increased delta-band functional connectivity (38 °C vs 21 °C), altered microstate D coverage, and increased relative delta source power with reduced beta and gamma source power in posterior and sensorimotor regions.

papers.title: Diagnosing Lennox-Gastaut syndrome in adulthood: A scoping review of diagnostic challenges and age-related electroclinical evolution.
papers.summary: This scoping review of 45 sources (421 patients) examined diagnostic challenges of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome in adulthood and the applicability of 2022 ILAE criteria. It found attenuation or under-documentation of classical features with age, including fulfillment of ILAE seizure-type criteria decreasing from 73% in childhood to 41% in adulthood, and mandatory EEG hallmarks documented in less than half of adults.

papers.title: Tri-Stream Disentangled Network with Adaptive Dual-Space Fusion for Electroencephalography-Based Image Reconstruction on THINGS-EEG2.
papers.summary: Presents a reproducible protocol for EEG-based image reconstruction using a Tri-stream Disentangled Network (TDE-Net) with adaptive dual-space fusion on THINGS-EEG2. Across 10 participants, TDE-Net achieved a mean CLIP pairwise identification accuracy of 0.8135, with ablation analyses characterizing the contributions of graph and semantic streams.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms of uncertain decision-making in anxious adolescents: an EEG study based on the balloon analogue risk task.
papers.summary: Anxious adolescents (n=20) and matched controls (n=20) performed a gain/loss Balloon Analogue Risk Task during EEG. Anxious adolescents showed behavioral avoidance (fewer pumps, lower BART scores) and distinct neural dynamics: elevated beta-band power and occipito-temporal connectivity during gain decisions, and increased theta-band parieto-temporal connectivity in loss contexts.

papers.title: EEG correlates of auditory rise time processing: A systematic review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA systematic review synthesized 37 EEG studies on auditory rise time (RT) processing in humans and found that RT prolongation consistently reduces ERP/brainstem/cortical response amplitudes and increases latencies; sensitivity varied along the auditory hierarchy, with earliest components tracking tens of microseconds and later components tracking changes up to 500 ms.

papers.title: Dissociable EEG microstate signatures of cognitive and response inhibition deficits in obsessive-compulsive disorder patients.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional study of 91 OCD patients and 76 healthy controls used resting-state EEG microstates to investigate neural correlates of cognitive and response inhibition deficits. OCD patients showed increased microstate A duration/coverage and decreased microstate C duration/occurrence/coverage, with microstate C duration positively correlated with stop-signal reaction time and microstate C/D metrics negatively correlated with Stroop effect, suggesting dissociable microstate signatures.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in drug-resistant epilepsy: A randomized, sham-controlled crossover trial with exploratory EEG and MRI response phenotyping.
papers.summary: In a randomized, sham-controlled crossover pilot trial of 14 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy, active transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation did not significantly outperform sham (mean seizure reduction ratio 46.26% vs 48.62%, difference -2.37%, p=0.604), but greater EEG beta-band attenuation in occipital and frontal regions was correlated with larger active-specific clinical benefit, and bilateral structural abnormalities/limbic involvement were more frequent among nonresponders.

papers.title: Design and Fabrication of an Anatomically Realistic Multimodal EEG/MEG Head Phantom.
papers.summary: The authors designed and fabricated a four-layer anatomically realistic desktop EEG/MEG head phantom using accessible materials, with skin and brain layer resistivities of 2.668 Ω·m each and average bulk skull resistivity of 169.2 Ω·m, and demonstrated simultaneous EEG and MEG recordings of dipole stimulations at four cortical locations producing biologically realistic scalp maps and signal amplitudes.

papers.title: Quantitative EEG and EEG-Derived Markers of Severity, Prognosis, and Recovery After Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 33 studies (1,696 participants) evaluated quantitative EEG and related biomarkers after ischemic stroke, finding that greater EEG abnormality—especially increased slow-wave activity, higher delta/alpha or delta-theta/alpha-beta ratios, and higher brain symmetry indices—was consistently associated with greater neurological severity, larger lesion burden, and poorer functional outcomes, though evidence certainty was low to very low and no universal prognostic threshold was supported.

papers.title: Heart rate fragmentation and variability from real-time cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging using TREND-CMR software.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
papers.summary: Developed TREND-CMR software to assess temporal variability in real-time cardiovascular magnetic resonance (rtCMR) using principal component analysis, adapting heart rate fragmentation (HRF) to rtCMR and introducing jerkiness and fragmentation of left ventricular filling time. Applied to 20 volunteers, the metrics suggested differences in two subjects with heart conditions and detected respiratory sinus arrhythmia-related beat alterations.

papers.title: Neurophysiological signatures of latent brain vulnerability in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: integrating EEG, cerebral oximetry, and processed EEG.
papers.summary: Narrative review examining EEG, NIRS/cerebral oximetry, and processed EEG/BIS as objective perioperative neuromonitoring markers for brain vulnerability in perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND). Suggests that reduced/slowed alpha activity, lower spectral edge frequency, altered theta activity, burst suppression, cerebral oxygen desaturation burden, rSO2 variability, and prolonged deep anesthesia may reflect different dimensions of vulnerability, but current evidence is limited and these are candidate markers rather than validated early-warning tools.

papers.title: Electroencephalography (EEG) and Quantitative EEG for Acute Stroke Triage and Post-Reperfusion Monitoring: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 15 studies evaluated EEG and quantitative EEG for acute ischemic stroke triage and post-reperfusion monitoring, finding promising but heterogeneous signals for acute stroke/TIA or large-vessel occlusion detection using slow-to-fast ratios, hemispheric asymmetry, and relative alpha/theta power, and for post-EVT/MT monitoring using QEEG slowing, frontal delta-alpha ratio, seizure detection, and neurovascular coupling, but no diagnostic domain was poolable and certainty was very low for diagnostic use.

papers.title: A case of acute lithium encephalopathy associated with elevated myelin basic protein levels in cerebrospinal fluid.
papers.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
papers.summary: A case report of a 50-year-old man with schizophrenia who developed acute lithium encephalopathy with coma after serum lithium reached 3.95 mEq/L, showing generalized rhythmic delta activity on EEG and elevated cerebrospinal fluid myelin basic protein (141 pg/mL) without pleocytosis or elevated IgG index, suggesting that toxic lithium exposure may induce central nervous system demyelination underlying prolonged neurological deficits.

papers.title: Multimodal neuromonitoring-guided cerebral protection and early neurocognitive outcomes after aortic arch surgery.
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort study (n=186) evaluated whether a multimodal neuromonitoring-guided cerebral-protection protocol was associated with lower cerebral physiological burden and improved early neurocognitive outcomes after open aortic arch surgery. The guided cohort had lower rSO2 burden, shorter EEG suppression, and shorter impaired autoregulation duration, with lower odds of postoperative delirium (OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.17-0.77) and 30-day cognitive decline (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.13-0.75).

papers.title: Axonal dysfunction precedes axonal degeneration in a mouse model of progressive parkinsonism
papers.summary: In the MitoPark mouse model of progressive parkinsonism, dopaminergic axons showed markedly reduced action potential-evoked calcium signals and impaired action potential propagation that emerged well before dopaminergic fiber loss and motor deficits. These findings identify early axon-specific physiological deficits that precede axonal degeneration.

papers.title: The Left Atrial Appendage: Anatomy, Electrophysiology, and Clinical Implications for Atrial Fibrillation and Stroke.
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent evidence on left atrial appendage anatomy, electrophysiology, imaging, and clinical implications, noting that high-resolution mapping identifies the LAA as a non-pulmonary-vein trigger in persistent/post-ablation AF and that the OPTION trial showed LAA closure after AF ablation was as effective as oral anticoagulation for preventing death, stroke, or systemic embolism with less non-procedure-related bleeding.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Approaches for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Diagnosis: Protocol for a Scoping Review.
papers.summary: Describes a scoping review protocol to map AI, machine learning, and deep learning approaches for ADHD diagnosis, covering data modalities, validation practices, and interpretability. The review will follow PRISMA-ScR and JBI guidelines, searching five databases for studies from January 2019 to April 2026.

papers.title: NA-CDQuant: Quantitative spectral analysis of nucleic acid structure by circular dichroism spectroscopy.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: The authors introduce NA-CDQuant, a framework that combines spectral deconvolution with a curated synchrotron radiation circular dichroism reference library of 18 structurally defined conformational families to quantitatively predict nucleic acid structure and estimate fractional composition of coexisting conformations in solution.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
